Privacy

Processed with Meta's Model API in Standard mode, which Meta's documentation says is not used to train Meta models. Uploads were set to expire after one hour and were deleted by Walkaround when the run ended. Model requests were sent with storage off. Meta's terms allow it to retain content for abuse review and legal reasons; Walkaround does not control that. SAM 3.1 saw the unblurred proxy for the length of one segmentation pass to find the plates and faces it then blurred. For the second look, two blurred crops per look were sent to Muse Spark Open on Baseten, a company separate from Meta; no video went there.

Files API upload deleted: 2026-11-01T07:19:49.948Z. Stored responses deleted: none stored or not yet. Quarantine (unblurred originals) deleted: 2026-11-01T07:19:49.948Z.

What to do with this sheet

  1. Start with the dated pickup frames in this sheet: the camera says not present, the file was received 2026-11-01T07:15:35.071Z, and the file hashes (0f6124176157, a157a4a7483b) are on page 1 and in the sealed manifest.
  2. Ask the company in writing for the full damage report, the repair estimate and every image it holds for this rental, including the pickup inspection images; Hertz says customers can request more images.
  3. Get an alternative written estimate from a body shop within 10 business days; card network rules compare two quotes (Visa Core Rules Table 5-19; Amex allows up to 115% of the estimate).
  4. If the company does not answer, escalate to a named executive and file a complaint with your state consumer protection office; the one sourced renter win came by executive escalation with the company's own scans.
  5. Last, the card dispute, with its clocks: 60 days from the statement under Regulation Z 1026.13, 120 days under Visa's rules, and the $50 cap of 15 USC 1666i; a dispute does not stop collections, so keep the paper trail.

L2 new or unseen: d is None for a return mark: new_or_unseen
K15 view flagged: Muse Spark flagged the pickup or return view of the panel wet, dirty or glare, so a mark seen in one walk only may be dirt, water or a reflection, or may have been hidden in the other walk; a mark in the same place in both walks keeps its label with a note
K2 single frame: the mark appears in 1 of 3 keyframes while the other two were complete and sharp
K4 uncertain type: type dirt, reflection or unsure

Method and limits

Every verdict on the panel pages was decided by code from the numbers below. The thresholds were frozen into this run under config hash 3fb220014a1d9911b5fd97f330fad75c426f3c5827c1a1a0e1bc3e1cb2506b7e. Rebuilding the derived files from the stored model answers and these thresholds gives the same bytes when the line below says so.

rebuildevent chain verified to the head on page 1 and any original still in quarantine re-hashed at sheet time; run walkaround verify to compare a rebuild
storageModel requests were sent with storage off and the models accepted it; nothing was kept after the run. Files API upload deleted: 2026-11-01T07:19:49.948Z; quarantine deleted: 2026-11-01T07:19:49.948Z.
Hertz thresholdsExample thresholds Hertz published (REV 7.2025), illustrative only, quoted from its Damage Charges support page saved 2026-10-26: a body scratch is billable when it cannot be covered by a credit card (2 in x 3.5 in), or when scratches over 1 in together exceed that area; a dent with a diameter over 1 in, or multiple dents; a wheel, rim or hubcap scratch or scuff over 1 in; any crack or chip in glass. Paint transfer or scuffs that do not break the paint are listed as Ordinary Wear and not charged.

Appendix B glossary

Glossary

already there: the same mark was found at pickup within tau_pre of its return position (rule L3).
needs your eye: a human should look; the pair sat in the band between tau_pre and tau_eye, or a cap (K1 to K15) applied (L4).
new or unseen: a return mark with no pickup mark near it; new, or not filmed at pickup (L2).
not seen at return: a pickup mark with no return mark near it (L1).
not comparable: a panel gate failed (G1, G3 to G10); both best frames still show with the reason (L6).
view flagged: Muse Spark said a frame shows water, dirt or glare. That is a model's judgment, so it no longer blocks a panel (gate G2 did that until Oct 31). A mark seen in one walk only is capped at needs your eye (K15); a mark in the same place in both walks keeps its label, with a note.
tight pair: a pair inside tau_pre is already there because the mark sits in the same place in both walks, whatever Muse Spark called it. So Spark's type (dirt, reflection or unsure, K4), the two types disagreeing (K5) and its low confidence (K12) are notes on that pair, and the second look compares the two crops and may lower it (K7). If the second look gives no answer, K4, K5 and K12 cap the pair at needs your eye as before. A mark seen in one walk only, or a pair in the band, keeps them as caps.
keyframe pair: each panel is compared on one pickup keyframe and one return keyframe. When that pair fails a gate of the pair (G3, G4, G5, G8 or G9), the panel's other keyframe pairs are tried in a fixed order (clean views first, then the two keyframe scores, then keyframe number) and the first that passes every gate is used. The panel page says which pair was used and what each pair tried failed. G1, G6, G7 and G10 belong to the panel, so no other pair can pass them.
outline changed in place: a panel that fails only the mask IoU gate (G4) on every keyframe pair tried, with the best IoU from 0.5 to under 0.7, is needs your eye (L7) instead of not comparable when the two keyframes' box shapes agree within 2% and the outline difference sits in one place (its largest blob holds at least half of it). A turned camera changes the box shape or spreads the difference along the whole outline; a crushed panel does neither. No marks are compared, so it never says already there or new.
counter-look: a mark seen in one walk only would be new or unseen (or not seen at return) on distance alone. If no cap already lowers it, the second look is shown the mark in its own walk and the other walk's view of the same panel with the spot where it would sit outlined (carried through the panel frame). If the look says the same mark shows there, or is unsure, it is needs your eye (K16, the other walk may show it); if it says different, or gives no answer, the label stands. A model can only lower a label.
units: panel-normalized distance; 1 unit is about 35 cm along a door (the about-cm beside it uses that).
tau_pre, tau_eye: the two distance thresholds, calibrated from the run's own repeat frames; printed on the method page.
Stays Put: a check that a mark moves with the panel through a short clip; a reflection slides, a scratch stays put.
sha256: the fingerprint of a file; one changed byte changes it.
sealed: the manifest of hashes was written and offered for time stamping before any model saw the video.
config hash: the fingerprint of every threshold the code used; it changes when a threshold changes.
rule id: the row of the decision table that produced a label; G gates a panel, K caps a mark, L names a label, E is a claim exit.

Appendix C verify it yourself

Verify it yourself (5 steps; none needs Walkaround's server)

1. Hash the video file on your phone or computer and compare it with page 1:
   shasum -a 256 <your video file>     (Linux: sha256sum <your video file>)
   pickup: 0f612417615726cf0bc5d0662a5373cdf92cd2defc7329e063685580a2fd04ed
   return: a157a4a7483b7540d1f4e133c1b69d7f51deeca9360336e96004e64fea2a7fed
2. Read the OpenTimestamps proof (pip install opentimestamps-client):
   ots info bundle/manifest.json.ots
3. Verify it against the Bitcoin block, or drop the .ots file on https://opentimestamps.org :
   ots verify bundle/manifest.json.ots
4. Verify the RFC 3161 token from freetsa (2026-11-01T07:15:41Z) with freetsa's certificates (download https://freetsa.org/files/cacert.pem and https://freetsa.org/files/tsa.crt):
   openssl ts -verify -data bundle/manifest.json -in bundle/manifest.json.tsr -CAfile cacert.pem -untrusted tsa.crt
5. Re-hash every file in the bundle and rebuild the derived files from the stored model answers:
   walkaround verify eval_nhtsa15759_r6
